title: Clarify press telegraphing and icon-only silent states
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Icon-only buttons and compact surfaces are producing inconsistent press feedback across themes and platform sizes. Some builds show an immediate opacity shift, others use a delayed ripple — both patterns have caused intermittent regressions in hit-target clarity and perceived latency. Goal: produce a single, audit-able spec that defines (1) the visual "press-telegraph" (micro-feedback) for primary/secondary/icon-only variants, (2) how reduced-motion/high-contrast modes override motion and opacity, and (3) a token migration plan so engineering can implement without introducing regressions. Deliverables: design spec, token mapping, implementation guidance for React/Native, QA checklist, and a small canary PR to validate across themes and mobile breakpoints.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Spec includes explicit CSS/token values for press start, active, and release states for Primary/Secondary/Ghost/Icon-only; 2) Reduced-motion and high-contrast behaviors are documented with example screenshots; 3) Token names are additive or have clear deprecation notes; 4) Engineering has a small test harness (storybook) exercising themes and edge cases; 5) No accessibility regressions: hit target >= 44x44, visible focus and ARIA labels preserved.
comments: 2026-03-09 - Aisha: Created ticket after investigating multiple regression reports from QA and a customer report where icon buttons appeared unresponsive on mobile. Linked initial screenshots from support thread: https://drive.redwood/support/icon-press-issue

2026-03-10 - Marco: Did a quick audit across Chrome/Safari/Android WebView. Observed that Ghost variants use `opacity: 0.85` on press while Icon-only uses transform scale(0.98) + 80ms transition. These mismatches explain perceived inconsistency. Added notes to Figma: https://figma.redwood/design-system/button-telegraphing

2026-03-11 - Aisha: Proposed decision: unify on visual telegraph that prioritizes clarity over motion — prefer a short opacity/overlay approach for icon-only (fast 40ms down, immediate restore) and reserve scale transforms for larger primary surface variants. Rationale: opacity is less likely to cause layout jitter and scales conflict with compact hitboxes.

2026-03-12 - UX Review (Leah Nguyen): Approved approach but requested explicit guidance for reduced-motion users: instead of opacity changes, use an instantaneous color overlay change with zero animation. Also called out focus ring contrast in high-contrast themes.

2026-03-12 - Eng feedback (Sanjay Rao): Engineering asks for tokenized durations and a compatibility shim for older consumers that still depend on scale-based press. Requested that new tokens be additive (eg. button.press.overlay-opacity) and not mutate button.* legacy tokens.

2026-03-13 - Aisha: Updated token proposal and added migration notes. Token mapping doc: https://confluence.redwood/design/button-telegraph-tokens. Included fallback CSS snippets for older browsers and sample React props for opt-in legacy behavior.

2026-03-14 - Marco: Implemented Storybook stories for all variants and themes on a branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/4897. Early QA found a regression in iOS Safari where transform + opacity combined created double-compositing causing jank; I removed transform for icon-only in the branch per decision.

2026-03-14 - QA (Nora Kim): Ran accessibility checks. Hit target check failed for icon-only compact at 32x32 in some legacy usage. Added follow-up task to align minimum hit target across tokens and create a shim that expands touch target without changing visual density.

2026-03-14 - Next steps (Aisha): 1) Finalize token names and add deprecation guide by 2026-03-17; 2) Engineering to run cross-platform canary for two days post-merge; 3) QA to rerun accessibility checklist on canary and report issues; 4) Schedule a short rollout announcement and docs update in the component library changelog.
notes: Trade-offs considered: scale transforms provide a stronger perceived press but cause compositing and layout instability in constrained containers; opacity overlays preserve layout but are subtler. Decision favors stability for compact/icon surfaces. Consider a follow-up to test haptics as a non-visual telegraph on mobile devices.
